headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.67 (95% CI: 0.51–0.88), suggesting that anti-inflammatory diet is associated with a lower risk of renal cell carcinoma. These findings were supported by moderate between-study heterogeneity (I² = 47.76%), suggesting some variability in the results across studies.
